title: World leaders descend on New York for UNGA — but who really has America’s ear?
summary: Over 100 world leaders descend on the United Nations General Assembly as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine dominate the diplomatic agenda.
story: Frank Ahrens says countries arriving for UNGA are competing not only for meetings in New York, but for attention, visibility and influence across the United States.

UNITED NATIONS, NEW YORK — More than 100 presidents and prime ministers will descend on New York this week for one of the busiest gatherings on the diplomatic calendar, arriving at a United Nations confronting wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, economic pressure from disrupted energy markets and fresh questions about the institution’s ability to respond to an increasingly fractured world.

The U.N. expects 73 heads of state and 45 heads of government, alongside 49 ministers, 11 vice presidents and one crown prince, U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric told reporters Friday. Member states have already submitted roughly 1,000 requests for bilateral meetings, while 168 events are scheduled during high-level week, according to Dujarric.
Asked Friday to characterize the atmosphere inside U.N. headquarters as the delegations prepare to arrive, Dujarric described it simply as "high stress."
INDIA'S MODI-IRAN MEETING COMES AMID US WARNINGS OF SANCTIONS ON TEHRAN'S TRADING PARTNERS
President Donald Trump addresses the 80th United Nations General Assembly at U.N. headquarters in New York City, Sept. 23, 2025. (REUTERS/Mike Segar)
The General Debate of the 81st U.N. General Assembly begins Tuesday, Sept. 22, under the theme, "Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all."

But beneath the speeches, motorcades and closed-door meetings across Manhattan is another competition: nearly every government represented in New York will be trying, in one way or another, to capture the attention of the United States.
"This is their moment to grab a piece of American mindshare for sure," Frank Ahrens, head of BGR Analytics, told Fox News Digital.
A new analysis released ahead of UNGA attempts to measure which countries already have it.

The 2026 BGR Impact Index, produced by BGR Analytics, the data practice of Washington-based BGR Group, ranks 197 countries and economies according to their overall footprint in the United States, combining economic, cultural, diplomatic, institutional and geopolitical measures. Japan holds the top position for a third consecutive year, followed by Germany, Canada, the United Kingdom and South Korea.
That competition is especially consequential this year.
TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS
President Donald Trump during the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York on Tuesday, Sept. 23, 2025. (David Dee Delgado/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

President Donald Trump will return to the General Assembly on Tuesday with the US-Iran war entering its seventh month, while fighting involving the Iran-backed Houthis has placed new pressure on shipping through the Red Sea and raised fresh concerns among Gulf states about regional security. Reuters reported Sept. 18 that European and Asian allies have largely resisted U.S. calls to become more directly involved in the Iran conflict and that the prolonged war has strained Washington’s relationships with some partners.

The stakes extend well beyond Iran. The General Assembly agenda is expected to be dominated also by Russia’s war against Ukraine, Israeli-Palestinian tensions, Sudan, climate change and artificial intelligence. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov are among the prominent leaders or representatives expected to speak.
That combination of military power, diplomatic access and public perception gets at the central question behind BGR’s index: what does influence actually mean?
BGR compiled more than 100 indicators, ranging from GDP, population and foreign investment to international students, cultural presence and lobbying activity in Washington.
But one of the most consequential variables in this year’s analysis came from a much newer arena: social media.

"We looked at 4.9 trillion pieces of data across an entire year because we know that a social media campaign can really move a country's perception in the U.S.," Ahrens said. "And that was really the big takeaway from this year's index."

Social-media sentiment accounts for 20% of the index, second only to cultural imprint at 24%. Institutional ties and outward orientation each make up 16%, geopolitical nexus accounts for 10%, economic size 8% and lobbying and Washington influence 6%. BGR says its underlying data comes from publicly available sources, primarily the U.N., U.S. government agencies and established research institutions, while its social-media data is supplied by Meltwater.
For smaller countries, the analysis suggests reputation can produce particularly large swings.

Bahrain was the biggest riser, climbing 22 places, from No. 97 in 2024 to No. 75 in 2026. BGR attributed much of that increase to improved U.S.-facing online sentiment and increased visibility tied to Bahrain’s election to a rotating U.N. Security Council seat, its Arabian Gulf Cup victory and a USS Nimitz port call.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM
United Nations headquarters during the 80th United Nations General Assembly, in New York City, New York, U.S., September 23, 2025. (REUTERS/Al Drago)

Georgia moved in the opposite direction, falling 31 positions, from No. 73 to No. 104. BGR said its deteriorating U.S.-facing online sentiment coincided with political unrest and arrests of journalists and opposition leaders.

Ahrens acknowledged that generating attention is not the same as wielding political influence. "Countries that make a lot of noise about themselves do get on the radar, but to stay on the radar, you have to have real accomplishments."

The index attempts to address that distinction by combining sentiment with harder measures such as economic links, institutional rankings, lobbying expenditure and participation in international organizations.
Perhaps BGR’s most unusual example of how national perception can change did not come from a president, diplomat or lobbying operation.
It came from a German soccer fan.
BGR calls it the "Freddy Effect," after a German World Cup visitor whose enthusiastic posts about traveling through the United States went viral this summer.

Ahrens said BGR found that positive sentiment toward Germany increased 13% over roughly three weeks during Freddy’s rise online. BGR links a substantial part of that increase to the reaction generated by his posts, although the data does not independently establish that he alone caused the change.
"Can you recreate a Freddy? I don't know if you can reverse engineer him to that effect," Ahrens said. "But what it shows you is how authentic communication really breaks through on social media."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

President Donald Trump (L) meets with United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres during the 80th session of the U.N. General Assembly (UNGA) at the United Nations headquarters on September 23, 2025, in New York City. World leaders convened for the 80th Session of UNGA, with this year’s theme for the annual global meeting being "Better together: 80 years and more for peace, development and human rights." (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

It is a lesson that may resonate with delegations arriving in New York this week, where hundreds of leaders will have only a few days to secure meetings, shape headlines and make their country’s case.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Bomb squad searching vans near U.S. air base in Britain after five men arrested
summary: LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terror and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S.
story: LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terror and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in west England.

The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base, and arrested five men “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act.” They were later further arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.

Police did not provide further details on the men, who remain in custody, or what they were suspected to have done. “Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing,” a police spokesperson said.
The force said 85 homes across the local area were evacuated and a 440-yard cordon put in place while an Army ordnance disposal team examines the vehicles.
Helicopter footage from Sky News showed multiple white vans close to the base seemingly being searched by a bomb disposal robot.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, told Britain’s Press Association another resident had reported three suspicious vans in the village. Along with other residents, Tudsbery has since been evacuated to a nearby recreation center.

The Reuters news agency had reported that security measures at the air ‌base have been significantly increased in recent ‌days. A spokesperson for the U.S. ‌Air Force told the agency they would not discuss specific force protection measures.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow ⁠UK-based Wings remain vigilant and ⁠will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security ‌of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the spokesperson ‌said, ahead of the police statement.
“We constantly assess ⁠a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families,” they added.
The British government said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being updated about the incident, adding “it would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.”
In March this year, Burnham’s predecessor Keir Starmer gave permission for the U.S. to use its bases for “specific and limited defensive” operations against Iran.

In July, Iran’s ⁠Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Britain that “any base used to invade Iranian territory is our legitimate target,” Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported, citing bomber aircraft flights from Fairford.
At the time, a British government spokesperson said that the country was “ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad.”

Roz Savage, the local member of Parliament, thanked police for their response to “worrying scenes just outside the RAF Fairford base,” while British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: “We can be reassured that this is being dealt with and it is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7.”

title: How an American teacher’s $5,000 donation helped turn a Chinese desert into a lush forest
summary: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.
story: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.

What was once a vast, dry desert in northern China has transformed into a lush, green forest of 50,000 full-grown trees, thanks in part to a $5,000 donation he made more than a quarter century ago to a local farmer and “sand-control worker” named Yin Yuzhen.
Sakolsky, 69, a retired teacher from Pennsylvania, was amazed to see the transformation in China’s Inner Mongolia region last month when he visited for the first time in 26 years.
“Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he told Chinese state media. “I saw pictures, I was told all about it, but until you see it is when you realize that it’s real.”

Sakolsky and Yin’s reunion last month has been held up by Chinese authorities as an example of how China and the United States, the world’s two biggest greenhouse gas emitters, can work together on global issues such as climate change.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping, in Washington this week for a summit with President Donald Trump, mentioned Sakolsky’s story in his toast at a state dinner on Thursday, saying it “touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between our two peoples.”

Sakolsky was teaching English on exchange in China’s central Henan province in 1999 when he saw a TV news report about Yin. More than a decade earlier, the newly married Yin had started planting trees as a way to feel less isolated in her new home in the Mu Us Desert, also known as the Maowusu Desert (“bad water” in Mongolian).

Moved by her story, Sakolsky raised $5,000, which was many times Yin’s annual income, so she could plant even more. They met in person in 2000, when Yin promised Sakolsky that she and her family would take good care of the saplings.

title: Anger grows across Spain after elderly woman evicted from her home of 70 years
summary: An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
story: An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted Wednesday from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years, in a case that highlights a growing housing crisis in the country.
Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who is a wheelchair user, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.

Supporters had gathered outside her building overnight on Friday, with dozens of police officers holding them back as some tried to stop the eviction from going ahead. In a social media video posted Friday by the Madrid tenants union, Abascal gave thanks for the support she had received.
Abascal’s lawyer, Beatriz Duro, described the force used in the eviction as “completely disproportionate and unnecessary” and decried the intransigence of the building’s owners.

The case has brought new attention to an ongoing housing crisis in major cities across Spain, as gentrification has caused rents to skyrocket and the stock of affordable housing to shrink, leading to fierce public anger.

On Saturday, tens of thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction, some setting off flares. They carried placards reading “Not one more eviction, not one less neighbor, we are all Maricarmen” and “right to housing at a fair price.”

At the end of the march, protesters sat down in the Puerta del Sol plaza, some pitching tents. They remained in place early Sunday as dozens of activists staged a sit-in. A model of a vulture, decrying so-called “vulture funds,” hung above the camp.
Earlier in the week, tenants unions and other housing groups held protests and rallies in 16 cities, including Granada, Logroño and Zaragoza.
An investment fund acquired Abascal’s building in 2018 and sought a steep increase in her rent, and she had been fighting eviction for more than five years, according to the Madrid tenants union.

Duro said court officials and representatives of the fund, Urbagestión, had refused to suspend the eviction despite a pending court filing, humanitarian appeals and evidence that public authorities were working to secure alternative accommodation.

“They’re all inhumane,” Abascal said in a Spanish television interview the day before her eviction. “It’s as if I’m living with a machete at the back of my neck, ready to be chopped off at any moment.”
Duro also said an anonymous individual had offered to cover the rent payments, but the landlord declined to sign a new lease.

“We’ve been trying to negotiate with the landlords right up until the last moment, and they’ve flatly refused everything,” she said, decrying “a lack of humanity” in her treatment and “all these public resources” channeled into enabling the eviction.
Urbagestión did not respond to a request for comment.

The fresh wave of anger comes after protests in recent years against overtourism in Barcelona, where activists say a surge in apartments being used for short-term vacation rentals has contributed to a shortage of affordable housing.
The European Union announced new rules earlier this month aimed at tackling the housing crunch caused by short-term rentals in tourism hot spots.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the eviction as “a social tragedy that we cannot accept either as a country or, of course, from the perspective of public institutions.”

Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Wednesday, Sánchez accused Madrid’s conservative regional government of pursuing luxury penthouses while ignoring demand for social housing.

Irene Hernández López, a 31-year-old test engineer living and renting in Chamberí, about 2 miles from Retiro, said what had happened to Abascal was “outrageous,” and she is worried similar evictions were already happening to other tenants around the city.
“Housing has become a product that people do business with,” she told NBC News. “It no longer matters that it’s your personal world, where you live and where you do your life.”

Hernández López, who pays 500 euros ($570) for a room in an apartment she shares with two others, said she was currently looking to move because the property was old and needs repairs, but that the rental market in Madrid was “terrible,” with prices “rising extremely quickly” and very little available.

“Some rooms are 500 euros or 600 euros and you think, ‘How am I supposed to live here? How can I pay 500 euros for this?’” she said. “I do think prices should be regulated, because wages aren’t going up while housing prices keep increasing. I don’t know how we’re supposed to keep going.”
Dan Nicander, secretary-general for the International Union of Tenants, said the situation in Spain was something his organization had seen in many countries in Europe.
“It’s a part of the financialization problem, seeing housing as an asset more than a home to people,” he told NBC News.

It’s “really tough” for the people living in the houses to do anything about it, he added, saying the responsibility lay with  politicians “to regulate the market in a way that it shouldn’t be that easy to buy and invest and then not [be] using the houses as homes.”
“Housing is a right,” he said. “It’s a fundamental right, first and foremost. It shouldn’t be a commodity.”

title: New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson kicks off the new season of ‘SNL’
summary: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live.”
story: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live.”
During Saturday’s hoops-heavy show, Brunson delivered a monologue in which he promised to approach his “SNL” performance with the same strategy he used during the Knicks’ Finals games.
“The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful,” he said. “The last sketch is going to be amazing.”

The monologue featured “SNL” veteran Kenan Thompson as ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith, invited by Brunson so the player could “get some closure” after Smith had expressed doubts about his abilities.
Jalen Brunson brings Knicks players to 'SNL'

“I am man enough to admit that I was wrong when the New York Knickerbockers signed you and I did not think that you were the answer,” Thompson’s Smith said. “Nor did I believe that you could deliver the team’s first championship since 1973, when I was only 5 years old.”
Knicks teammates Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns made cameos to portray members of the studio audience chosen to ask questions of the point guard.
“Can you foul out of ‘SNL’?” Towns asked.

In the recorded sketch “High School Musical the New Generation,” Brunson played a new student who wanted to join the school’s basketball team. He was welcomed with a musical number on the court that culminated with a team member portrayed by “SNL” featured player Jeremy Culhane singing that he was about to “take the shot.”

It was at that point that his attempt at scoring was rejected by Brunson, with the ball slamming against his forehead. Each subsequent attempt at a basket by Culhane’s character was met with an over-the-top rejection. Soon, Brunson was defeating the team by weaving through defender traffic and scoring easily.

The NBA player concluded by swooping in to steal Culhane’s love interest (played by featured player Veronika Slowikowska) during another musical number, showing that even his singing chops were better than Culhane’s character’s. “Yeah, I think I’m going to hook up with this guy,” Slowikowska’s character said of the new student.
Brunson is the fifth NBA star to host the storied sketch comedy show, joining coach Bill Russell and legendary players Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James in sharing that status.
He averaged 32.6 points per game in the NBA Finals to help his team win its first championship in 53 years.

Saturday’s show also marked the first “SNL” season for two new featured players, Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter, after it bid farewell to cast member Chloe Fineman and writer Martin Herlihy, who also appeared in a number of sketches.

Fineman landed a role on “Myron Bolitar,” a Netflix drama series based on Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about a former basketball star who reinvents himself as a sports agent. Netflix announced the show started filming in New York City in July.

The musical guest Saturday was Katseye, the K-pop-influenced act composed of six women from around the world but often performing as a quintet and quartet due to hiatuses. The act was put together under a partnership between Geffen Records and South Korea’s HYBE Entertainment, home of BTS.
Katseye performed a pair of songs, “Animal” and “Hootie Frutti,” and appeared as judges in a recorded sketch that spoofed Season 2 of the talent competition TV show “The Debut: Dream Academy.”
“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

title: It’s cute. It’s cuddly. And it wants your data.
summary: Meta is touting its new personal AI agent, Muse, as a product “built for everyone” — including those who lack experience with technology.
story: Meta hopes its new AI agent will win people over by being cute.
Muse, the tech giant’s cuddly, doll-like AI agent, shot to the top of the Apple App Store charts after it was featured this week at the company’s Meta Connect conference.
The company is touting the tool, designed to help people with their everyday tasks, as an AI agent “built for everyone,” including those who lack experience with technology.
AI agents, which are systems that automatically execute tasks on a user’s behalf, are rapidly becoming ubiquitous in online workspaces, social apps and personal devices.
Meet Mark Zuckerberg's personal Muse AI agent

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the default Muse avatar, which is cream-colored and has beady black eyes and an upward smile, is named “Jolly,” for its “jolly and completely customizable character and personality.”

Muse is being launched as tech companies seek to make their AI-powered products more palatable to humans, often by giving them cute, almost petlike appearances, voices and personalities. Experts have said design choices that humanize technology may become more common as robot-human interaction grows more prevalent in everyday spaces, as cuteness evokes “deep-seated biological responses” in people.

“It was only about six months ago that having a personal agent running on your own computer was the sign of someone who is completely AI-pilled and thinking nonstop about agents,” Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, said Wednesday. “But for that small group of nerds ... it looked like the beginning of personal superintelligence. And today with Muse, we’ve brought that magic to everyone.”

Muse agents can take on a variety of appearances, with users able to customize everything from their names to their attire. Zuckerberg’s agent, which wears a toga and a wreath around its head, is named Agrippa, after the Roman general and statesman.

During the event, Zuckerberg also teased what he calls the “Muse charm,” a small handheld device that can activate the agent on the go. He raised the keychain charm onstage at Meta Connect in Menlo Park, California, showing off what looks like a blend of a Labubu and a Tamagotchi.

“Talking to your Muse is often the fastest way to get things done, and it is also just really fun and cute,” he said, saying he used Agrippa to come up with a baking recipe and order ingredients for him and his daughter.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Muse is also being integrated directly into Meta’s expanding lineup of AI-powered glasses, which have been criticized over fears of casual surveillance. Zuckerberg has told NBC News that Meta will continue to bolster privacy safeguards for its smart glasses.

Zuckerberg said every Muse agent has its own private and secure computer called Muse Secure VM, a dedicated secure computer that houses both the agent and the user’s personal data. Down the line, he said, Meta plans to release Muse Confidential VM “so that even Meta won’t be able to see that information.”

“In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives,” he said.
Online, the reaction has been mixed.
Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, posted a flurry of memes inserting Muse into moments from movies, shows and historical events.
Some followed his lead by making their own avatars and sharing screenshots on social media.
Others, however, expressed skepticism, citing security concerns.
“Am I the only one who doesn’t want to let meta have access to my whole life?” a user posted.
“We are going to need some tight defenses and 3rd party testing of these platforms... like all software products,” entrepreneur and angel investor Jason Calacanis wrote.

Zuckerberg has continued to be bullish on AI despite recent calls from tech executives and government officials to pump the brakes on AI development amid surging fears about the existential risk the technology poses.
He shared his thoughts recently on X, saying market forces should be enough to keep AI companies in line.

“My view is that trust and alignment are quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models. Any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind,” he wrote, adding: “Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would.”

title: Should you bring iced coffee to a job interview? Question brews generational debate
summary: What started as a conversation about job interview tips online escalated into a generational debate over whether it’s taboo to show up with an iced coffee to talk to a potential employer.
story: What started as a conversation about job interview tips online escalated into a generational debate over whether it’s taboo to show up with an iced coffee to talk to a potential employer.

The discourse over the caffeinated beverage gained momentum on TikTok this week after a creator, who goes by @caitlinrecruiter on the platform, shared a video in which she said she believes “when you show up with an iced coffee or an iced latte that this interview is just a stop on your list of errands for the day.”
“It looks a little too casual to me,” she said in the video, which she posted Sept. 16.

Caitlin Wehniainen, whose profile states she has 16 years of recruiting experience, has just over 1,000 followers on TikTok. But in the last week, her video has been clipped and recirculated by dozens of creators online, who engaged in a heated back-and-forth about whether she’s right.
The divide seemed to primarily be between younger and older users — with the former group suggesting Wehniainen’s tip “makes no sense at all” and that such a perspective is archaic.

Others, many who identified as Gen Xers in comments, agreed with Wehniainen, writing that “arguing against this is insane” and telling applicants that they should “save the iced coffee for when you actually get hired.”

By Monday, even the coffee giant Starbucks had taken a side, alluding to the debate in an Instagram post that featured an image of someone holding an iced coffee in one hand and sunglasses and their handbag in the other. “Pulling up to the interview like,” the caption read. Meanwhile, The Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, another coffee chain, commented on Wehniainen’s video: “We’d hire them on spot...”
When reached for comment on Friday, Wehniainen said in an email to NBC News that she was “shocked at how polarizing the topic is.”

“But I realize that the original message was taken out of context as the virality of the post grew,” she wrote. “As the topic spread, many decided to weigh in with their own general opinion on whether or not bringing an iced coffee into an interview is appropriate ... I also saw people reading into it too much, asking if coffee or water matters and what is appropriate. I will say, I think a bottled water is great to bring with you.”

The timing of the conversation coincides with a tough job market: Recent college graduates are facing higher unemployment rates than other age groups as it’s becoming more difficult to obtain entry-level jobs, NBC News reported last month. Employers are not looking to add talent, and employed people are not moving to new positions, as a rise in AI continues to threaten jobs.

For Los Angeles-based TikTok creator Esha, who preferred to be identified by only her first name, citing privacy concerns, Wehniainen’s words couldn’t be further from the truth. She was among the many weighing in online, telling her 81,000-plus TikTok followers that “the iced coffee controversy completely misunderstands interviews.”

“Thinking of a job interview as a stop in your day is very normal,” Esha, 22, added in an interview with NBC News, noting that she’s brought iced coffees to several interviews and hasn’t thought twice about it.
“Gen Z had this shift in recent years, where we can still have a life outside of work,” Esha said. “So, like, why am I changing who I am? Why am I missing my coffee for the day for this interview?”
In her video, she elaborated further on her take, saying that “the most easily relatable thing in corporate America is a coffee addiction.”

“Unless you’re like over the age of 30 and you can relate on having kids, and doing stuff with your kids, coffee is the main thing. Everyone’s like, ‘Gotta get that coffee’ ... and finding something personable about a person is so important,” she said. “Like, who is not starting their workday off with a coffee?”
Catherine Fisher, vice president of communications at LinkedIn, said she’s not surprised by the generational divisions when it comes to job etiquette.

“Gen Z is entering this workforce at such a challenging time, it’s such a competitive job market, and to then get judged by bringing an iced coffee just seems like, ‘Have we lost the plot here?’” she said.
That said, Fisher is among the cohort who believes it’s best to skip the iced coffee when headed to an interview.

“Even though I don’t like the answer, I think because everyone is so divided on it, I would be cautious and not bring one,” she said. “You just don’t know who’s on the other side of the interview, so why risk it over something so silly?”
Etiquette expert Thomas Farley, who is known as Mister Manners to his followers online, agreed with the more traditional point of view.

“I think it sends the wrong message in so many respects,” he said. “I think it shows you to be someone who didn’t plan your time accordingly, and you’re multitasking, and that’s not what you should be doing during the interview.”
Farley also warned of the physical pratfalls a coffee could bring.
“There are real practical considerations when you bring a liquid into someone’s office,” he said. “Where does it go? What happens if you spill it?”
While he doesn’t think it should be the deciding factor for any hiring manager, Farley argued candidates should be doing everything in their power to leave a positive impression.

“If it’s between you and three other people, and everyone’s qualifications are more or less equal, and that’s the one thing that potentially sinks your chance to get the job, I think that would be really unfortunate,” he said. “That would be a very expensive $7 cup of iced coffee.”
Still, Gen Zers like Esha are not convinced that bringing the beverage would make or break their job opportunity.
As another TikTok creator put it in their video: “It’s really, really not that serious most of the time.”
As for Wehniainen? Even after the online uproar, she said her “opinion still stands that you shouldn’t bring an iced coffee to your interview.”
“You want to leave outlying distractions like iced coffee behind,” she said, “and connect with your interviewer with full attention.”

title: Bill Gates says getting countries to agree on AI regulations will be harder than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations
summary: Bill Gates called on the U.S. to lead in the global regulation of AI growth but warned agreeing on a global AI regulation could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations.
story: Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates called on the U.S. to be a leader in regulating the growth of artificial intelligence but warned that getting countries to agree on a global framework could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era negotiations to limit nuclear weapons.
“This is more difficult than that was,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Wednesday during a wide-ranging discussion on AI that aired Sunday.

His remarks came as he spoke about President Donald Trump’s stance against regulating AI. The president earlier this month rejected calls for the federal government to impose guardrails for companies building AI models, saying in a post on Truth Social, “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”
Gates argued Wednesday that regulating AI companies by imposing monitoring systems would not hamper the U.S. in any race with China to develop superior technology.

“What he said is fine, but I think after he hears from me and other people, including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is, that, you know, we will come to a consensus,” the tech mogul said.
Gates later pointed to other times the U.S. has led the world in coming up with broad agreements to protect humanity.

“Since World War II, the U.S. should be very proud that when there have been global challenges, we, in a way that was benign, where we had friends and allies coming along with us, you know, aviation safety, ozone layer, nuclear weapons, a lot of things where we played the fair actor, not aggrandizing whatever our unique strengths were,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “And AI is one we’re going to have to go back to this, ‘Hey, humanity is all in this together.’”

Concerns about AI reached a fever pitch this month after Jacob Coxon, a whistleblower who had recently resigned from Anthropic, issued a public warning: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Days later, two of the nation’s leading AI CEOs — Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Sam Altman of OpenAI — agreed there is a need to slow the pace of AI development amid fears the tech would soon be capable of “superintelligence” that outpaces human thinking.

In a blog post, Amodei wrote that “frontier” AI companies must slow down the pace of AI development but only to a point where the companies still lead China. He also urged global coordination between democratic and authoritarian governments to create regulations.

In recent weeks, both companies have announced plans to track the behavior of AI agents after OpenAI flagged multiple incidents in which its agents behaved in a concerning way, including by hacking an outside company without being told to do so.

In a post on Truth Social ahead of a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Trump wrote: “Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China’s position also.”
Addressing immediate concerns about AI

While many have been calling for regulations that would limit AI from destroying humanity, Gates said on “Meet the Press” that he believes there should be guardrails in place to prevent mass-casualty events that could be coordinated with the help of AI today.

“The most dangerous thing we’re facing right now is people with bad intent using AI. You know, so somebody who wants to defraud an individual or wants to shut down the electric network or scramble bank accounts, they are now empowered,” the philanthropist said.

“Historically, countries had cyberattack teams and they could think of things like bioterror weapons,” he said. “Now, small groups with AI can do what only the biggest countries could do. So it’s really the bad intent plus AI that looms as a major threat. Unless governments insist on various safeguards, you know, we will see a lot of big, negative things because we’re not safeguarding.”
Gates specifically said monitoring, “where you’re watching what the AI is doing,” is an important safeguard to introduce in each AI lab.

“Law enforcement is going to get called up on all these fraud events or, you know, transmission shutdown events,” he added. “And their ability to see what’s going on is going to be nil unless the monitoring and safeguards are built into the AI.”
Plus, Gates said, these kinds of safety features can be added to current AI systems without slowing down the pace of development.

“That’s another debate — of should we slow down or not,” he said. “But deciding to put the safeguards and monitoring in, that’s a choice we have. And the only question is, Do we do that before or after there’s some large-scale cyberattacks or bioattacks?”
One bipartisan proposal in Congress would require a “kill switch,” or a way for AI companies to immediately suspend or shut down their AI services if a dangerous situation occurs.
Gates said “it’s not enough to have a kill switch” and renewed his calls for internal monitoring and safeguards.

“I would never want to say I’m against a kill switch,” he added. “But when you’re trying to moderate the bad behavior, you need insight and records of what’s being done. So the kill switch alone would not prevent these tragedies.”
The Gates Foundation and AI
The philanthropist, who now leads the Gates Foundation, also spoke about the group’s work expanding AI access to countries where English isn’t the primary language.

“AI models have gotten very good at recognizing English and about a dozen other mainstream languages. And so as you talk about your health, it’s going to accurately record that and be able to help you. In African languages, the error rate will be about 10 times higher,” he said, adding that errors can be “very dangerous.”
The Gates Foundation, he added, is working with 60 AI companies to expand the reliable languages they offer.

“We have a very concrete timeline to improve the quality, to benchmark and then say, ‘OK, this is good enough. You can do a health interview or an education session in this language,’” he added, saying he hopes that within five years every language that a million or more people speak will be close to the quality of English on these platforms.
Gates said his foundation is also using AI in its own work.

“It’s helping me in the foundation work,” he said. “You know, ‘What’s the latest on malaria? What’s the latest on malnutrition?’ It’s allowing the Gates Foundation, which will spend all its money over the next 19 years — you know, it’s got a bit over $200 billion — that money will be far, far better spent because we’re using AI to guide our work.”
A ‘regrettable’ relationship with Jeffrey Epstein

In the last year, Gates has also faced scrutiny for his ties to the late Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender. When the Justice Department released a trove of files related to Epstein at the direction of federal lawmakers, Gates’ name appeared multiple times, including in emails from Epstein suggesting that Gates had extramarital affairs.
The Microsoft co-founder has since called his past relationship with Epstein “foolish” and testified to House lawmakers in June that he did not engage in illegal activity with Epstein.
On Wednesday, Gates accused Epstein of using their friendship to boost his reputation.

“I was told by Jeffrey after I met him that he could help raise billions of dollars for global health — you know, he wouldn’t be paid, he would have no role. That proved to be a complete dead end. So my spending time with him, like many other people, kind of helped his reputation. You know, that’s very regrettable,” he said.

title: Bomb squad searching vans near U.S. air base in Britain after five men arrested
summary: LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terror and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S.
story: LONDON — British police arrested several men on suspicion of terror and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in west England.

The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base, and arrested five men “on suspicion of committing offenses under the Explosives Act.” They were later further arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.

Police did not provide further details on the men, who remain in custody, or what they were suspected to have done. “Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing,” a police spokesperson said.
The force said 85 homes across the local area were evacuated and a 440-yard cordon put in place while an Army ordnance disposal team examines the vehicles.
Helicopter footage from Sky News showed multiple white vans close to the base seemingly being searched by a bomb disposal robot.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, told Britain’s Press Association another resident had reported three suspicious vans in the village. Along with other residents, Tudsbery has since been evacuated to a nearby recreation center.

The Reuters news agency had reported that security measures at the air ‌base have been significantly increased in recent ‌days. A spokesperson for the U.S. ‌Air Force told the agency they would not discuss specific force protection measures.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow ⁠UK-based Wings remain vigilant and ⁠will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security ‌of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the spokesperson ‌said, ahead of the police statement.
“We constantly assess ⁠a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families,” they added.
The British government said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being updated about the incident, adding “it would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.”
In March this year, Burnham’s predecessor Keir Starmer gave permission for the U.S. to use its bases for “specific and limited defensive” operations against Iran.

In July, Iran’s ⁠Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned Britain that “any base used to invade Iranian territory is our legitimate target,” Iran’s semiofficial Tasnim news agency reported, citing bomber aircraft flights from Fairford.
At the time, a British government spokesperson said that the country was “ready to keep the United Kingdom safe from any kind of attacks, whether it’s on our soil or from abroad.”

Roz Savage, the local member of Parliament, thanked police for their response to “worrying scenes just outside the RAF Fairford base,” while British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: “We can be reassured that this is being dealt with and it is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7.”

title: How an American teacher’s $5,000 donation helped turn a Chinese desert into a lush forest
summary: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.
story: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.

What was once a vast, dry desert in northern China has transformed into a lush, green forest of 50,000 full-grown trees, thanks in part to a $5,000 donation he made more than a quarter century ago to a local farmer and “sand-control worker” named Yin Yuzhen.
Sakolsky, 69, a retired teacher from Pennsylvania, was amazed to see the transformation in China’s Inner Mongolia region last month when he visited for the first time in 26 years.
“Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he told Chinese state media. “I saw pictures, I was told all about it, but until you see it is when you realize that it’s real.”

Sakolsky and Yin’s reunion last month has been held up by Chinese authorities as an example of how China and the United States, the world’s two biggest greenhouse gas emitters, can work together on global issues such as climate change.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping, in Washington this week for a summit with President Donald Trump, mentioned Sakolsky’s story in his toast at a state dinner on Thursday, saying it “touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between our two peoples.”

Sakolsky was teaching English on exchange in China’s central Henan province in 1999 when he saw a TV news report about Yin. More than a decade earlier, the newly married Yin had started planting trees as a way to feel less isolated in her new home in the Mu Us Desert, also known as the Maowusu Desert (“bad water” in Mongolian).

Moved by her story, Sakolsky raised $5,000, which was many times Yin’s annual income, so she could plant even more. They met in person in 2000, when Yin promised Sakolsky that she and her family would take good care of the saplings.

title: New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson kicks off the new season of ‘SNL’
summary: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live.”
story: NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live.”
During Saturday’s hoops-heavy show, Brunson delivered a monologue in which he promised to approach his “SNL” performance with the same strategy he used during the Knicks’ Finals games.
“The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful,” he said. “The last sketch is going to be amazing.”

The monologue featured “SNL” veteran Kenan Thompson as ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith, invited by Brunson so the player could “get some closure” after Smith had expressed doubts about his abilities.
Jalen Brunson brings Knicks players to 'SNL'

“I am man enough to admit that I was wrong when the New York Knickerbockers signed you and I did not think that you were the answer,” Thompson’s Smith said. “Nor did I believe that you could deliver the team’s first championship since 1973, when I was only 5 years old.”
Knicks teammates Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns made cameos to portray members of the studio audience chosen to ask questions of the point guard.
“Can you foul out of ‘SNL’?” Towns asked.

In the recorded sketch “High School Musical the New Generation,” Brunson played a new student who wanted to join the school’s basketball team. He was welcomed with a musical number on the court that culminated with a team member portrayed by “SNL” featured player Jeremy Culhane singing that he was about to “take the shot.”

It was at that point that his attempt at scoring was rejected by Brunson, with the ball slamming against his forehead. Each subsequent attempt at a basket by Culhane’s character was met with an over-the-top rejection. Soon, Brunson was defeating the team by weaving through defender traffic and scoring easily.

The NBA player concluded by swooping in to steal Culhane’s love interest (played by featured player Veronika Slowikowska) during another musical number, showing that even his singing chops were better than Culhane’s character’s. “Yeah, I think I’m going to hook up with this guy,” Slowikowska’s character said of the new student.
Brunson is the fifth NBA star to host the storied sketch comedy show, joining coach Bill Russell and legendary players Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James in sharing that status.
He averaged 32.6 points per game in the NBA Finals to help his team win its first championship in 53 years.

Saturday’s show also marked the first “SNL” season for two new featured players, Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter, after it bid farewell to cast member Chloe Fineman and writer Martin Herlihy, who also appeared in a number of sketches.

Fineman landed a role on “Myron Bolitar,” a Netflix drama series based on Harlan Coben’s thriller novels about a former basketball star who reinvents himself as a sports agent. Netflix announced the show started filming in New York City in July.

The musical guest Saturday was Katseye, the K-pop-influenced act composed of six women from around the world but often performing as a quintet and quartet due to hiatuses. The act was put together under a partnership between Geffen Records and South Korea’s HYBE Entertainment, home of BTS.
Katseye performed a pair of songs, “Animal” and “Hootie Frutti,” and appeared as judges in a recorded sketch that spoofed Season 2 of the talent competition TV show “The Debut: Dream Academy.”
“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

title: San Francisco Giants’ ‘mom of the year’ defends husband after clip sparks online backlash
summary: A woman Giants announcers dubbed “mom of the year” after cameras caught her carrying a baby and an armful of food back to her seat while a man beside her began eating is saying the viral clip didn’t show the whole story.
story: A woman Giants announcers dubbed “mom of the year” after cameras caught her carrying a baby and an armful of food back to her seat while a man beside her began eating is saying the viral clip didn’t show the whole story.
“Before you decide what our marriage looks like, I would like you to hear from the woman you’re defending,” she wrote.

The woman, who identified herself as Erika, described what happened at Tuesday’s San Francisco Giants game in a Substack post Friday. She said she had taken their daughter to the restroom and offered to pick up food for her husband, Ramses, on the way back. He told her to get him whatever had the shortest line.

When she returned, Ramses asked whether she wanted to eat first, Erika wrote. She told him to go ahead because she had eaten before the game and knew he had not had a full meal that day. He also offered to take the food containers off her lap and share his sandwich, but she declined.

Giants announcers Mike Krukow and Duane Kuiper narrated the scene as the camera lingered on the family. They dubbed Erika “mom of the year” and jokingly imagined that Ramses had asked her for ketchup and that she wanted to smack him. Erika said neither exchange happened.
“I understand how it looked on television,” she wrote. “But we could hear each other. The announcers and audience couldn’t.”

The was another reason Erika wanted Ramses to enjoy the game, she said. He had recently lost a childhood friend who was a gifted baseball player, and she had suggested the outing as a way for her husband to remember him.
“The camera showed what I was carrying in my hands,” she wrote. “It couldn’t show what he was carrying that night.”

Erika said she and Ramses initially laughed at the broadcast. But as the clip spread online, strangers began criticizing him and making assumptions about their marriage. Some found the couple’s names and phone numbers, she wrote, and some sent Ramses messages telling him to kill himself.
Erika said she believed that the announcers and Giants production team meant no harm. But she told them their jokes helped turn her husband into a source of ridicule.
“What was a few moments of amusement on your broadcast became days of real pain for our family,” she wrote.
A Giants spokesperson did not return a request for comment.
Erika said she appreciated being called “mom of the year” but asked people to listen when she described her own life.
“You can appreciate what I was doing that night without assuming I have to do everything alone,” she wrote. “Supporting me also means listening when I tell you about my own life.”

title: Carrot Top released from hospital after suicide attempt, rep says
summary: Carrot Top has been released from the hospital following treatment after a suicide attempt last week, a representative for the comedian confirmed to NBC News on Saturday.
story: Carrot Top has been released from the hospital following treatment after a suicide attempt last week, a representative for the comedian confirmed to NBC News on Saturday.
The 61-year-old performer, whose real name is Scott Thompson, was hospitalized after the Sept. 18 attempt. Further details about the medical emergency have not been made public.
“His family and those closest to him are deeply grateful for the concern, prayers and respectfully ask for privacy,” a spokesperson for the comedian said in a statement last week.

The hospitalization comes amid contentious civil litigation involving the comedian. In court filings, Carrot Top’s lawyers have accused singer-entertainer Brian Evans of trying to extort their client — allegedly demanding large payouts while threatening to expose embarrassing information, “false allegations” and “salacious materials.” Evans claims to have appeared as an opening act for Carrot Top’s Las Vegas show.

Following the suicide attempt, Carrot Top’s lawyers asked the judge overseeing the case to limit what Evans, who is representing himself, could file on the public docket, arguing that the release of “intensely private material on a docket monitored by national media” would cause irreparable harm.
Carrot Top rose to fame in the 1990s for his curly red mane and loud wardrobe, and has remained  a pop culture figure for decades.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7, to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Neighbor charged with murder after Georgia DoorDash driver found dismembered
summary: Police in Smyrna, Georgia, said Friday they found the dismembered remains of a woman stuffed into garbage bags inside a car trunk at an apartment complex this week.
story: Police in Smyrna, Georgia, said Friday they found the dismembered remains of a woman stuffed into garbage bags inside a car trunk at an apartment complex this week.
The victim, Shanteria Mosley — known to family and friends as “KT” — worked as a DoorDash delivery driver. Investigators said one of the bags “was pulled tightly showing the outline of a body part.”
An 18-year-old who lived at the same apartment complex has been charged with her murder.

“This is a shocking crime. I don’t know how else to describe it,” Lt. Meredith Holt, the public information officer for the Smyrna Police Department, said at a press conference on Friday. “I’ve been in law enforcement for 25 years, and I have been a part of multiple homicide cases, and I worked crimes against children for 16 years, and this is a particularly gruesome crime.”
“I cannot imagine what the family is going through,” Holt added.
Mosley’s body was discovered while checking the car at Park Valley Apartments in response to a missing person report earlier in the week.
Authorities waited for officials from the Cobb County medical examiner’s office to arrive at the complex before opening the bags to confirm they contained body parts, according to a news release.
Kingston Bradley of Smyrna, Georgia, was arrested and charged with concealing the death of another and malice murder in connection with Mosley’s death.
Police said Bradley lives with his father at Park Valley Apartments, where the body was found.

Holt did not say whether Bradley and Mosley knew each other prior to the incident but said authorities are still investigating how the two were connected. Holt said the victim was not working the day she was killed.
Neither DoorDash nor family members for Mosley immediately returned requests for comment.

title: Love to Dream just recalled this popular sound machine
summary: Love to Dream recalled its portable baby sound machine over a battery fire and burn risk. Here’s how to check your model and date code and get a refund.
story: If you use a Love to Dream sound machine to help your baby drift off, you’ll want to pay attention to this news: The brand has recalled their portable white noise machine because its lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging with an incompatible charger, posing a risk of fire and burns. Below, find everything you need to know about the recall, including how to check whether your sound machine is affected.
Why was the Love to Dream sound machine recalled?

Love to Dream recalled its Sleep Machine because the device’s lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging if it’s connected to a charger that isn’t compatible with the unit. That overheating poses a risk of injury from fire and burns, a serious concern for a product that’s often kept in a nursery.

The recall applies only to the Love to Dream Sleep Machine with model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN. The recalled product is a white, heart-shaped portable white noise machine with a night light and a tan carry strap. You can find the date code printed on the side of the machine or on the back of its box, and Love to Dream says units with any other date code are not affected and aren’t part of the recall.

The affected machines were sold from February 2025 through September 2026, and Love to Dream is conducting the recall in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The company’s recall notice doesn’t say how many units are affected or whether any overheating incidents or injuries have been reported.
What to do if you have the recalled sound machine

If your Love to Dream Sleep Machine has model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN, stop using it immediately. Disconnect it from any charger and put it somewhere safe, away from anything flammable or anything that could damage it. Then visit lovetodream.com/recall to find out how to dispose of the device and claim your refund. Because the machine contains a lithium-ion battery, you should not toss it in your household trash or recycling bin. Instead, dispose of it only according to your local requirements for lithium-ion products.
If you have questions, you can contact Love to Dream by email at recall@lovetodream.com or by calling toll-free at 1-833-753-3710.
Other portable sound machines to use instead
The below portable sound machines have not been recalled and can be safely used.
Hatch Go Portable Sound Machine

The Hatch Go is a rechargeable sound machine for babies on the go. It plays 10 soothing sounds, like white noise and heartbeat, and has three buttons plus a ring to clip onto a stroller or diaper bag. It needs no app, WiFi or Bluetooth, and lasts up to 15 hours per charge.
Yogasleep Hushh Portable White Noise Sound Machine

The Yogasleep Hushh is a compact portable sound machine with three sounds: bright white noise, deep white noise and gentle surf. It weighs just 3.8 ounces, has an amber night light and child lock, and clips onto a stroller, car seat or crib. It runs up to 24 hours per charge.
Momcozy Portable Sound Machine with Night Light

With 20 soothing sounds and an amber night light you can dim, this portable machine from Momcozy works for nursery and travel alike. It clips onto a stroller, crib or diaper bag, and includes a timer, child lock and auto shut-off. It charges via USB-C and is designed to last all night.

title: This is how often you should be cleaning your makeup brushes, according to experts
summary: Dirty makeup brushes can cause breakouts and irritation. Experts share how often to clean your brushes and sponges, plus the best cleaners to get the job done.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans.

Makeup brushes do a lot of work — namely sweeping foundation, blush, powder and other cosmetics onto your face day after day — yet many people rarely think about cleaning them. It’s an easy chore to put off, especially since freshly washed brushes can take up to 24 hours to dry. The only problem with that is that skipping regular cleanings can affect both how your makeup looks and the health of your skin.

“[Not cleaning makeup brushes] can lead to makeup buildup on the brush hairs, which can negatively affect the softness of the bristles over time and lead to a patchy or streaky application,” says Eric Vosburg, a New York City-based makeup artist. “And due to the high moisture content from liquid and cream products, bacteria can easily form and grow, which can cause the contaminated tools to spread bacteria around the skin, leading to acne.”

So, how often should you actually be washing them? I posed that very question to Vosburg and other professional makeup artists and got tips on the best way to actually wash them and recommendations on tools that can help you get the job done.
How often should you clean your makeup brushes?

How often you should wash your makeup brushes depends on how frequently you use them and what you use them for. As a general rule, Vosburg recommends cleaning them once a week to reduce product buildup and keep bristles in good condition. Brushes used with liquid or cream formulas, like foundation and concealer, tend to collect residue and moisture faster than those used with powders, so they need attention more frequently — you may be able to stretch wash time on powder brushes to every two weeks.

Certain situations also call for extra cleanings. If you’ve recently been sick, wash your brushes once you’ve recovered to avoid transferring germs back onto your skin or into your makeup products. And if you’re dealing with acne or breakouts, more frequent cleaning can help limit the spread of bacteria and fungus and prevent reinfection, says Zac Hart, a New York City-based hair and makeup artist.

Between deep cleanings, a quick-dry brush cleaner can be a convenient option, since it removes residue and sanitizes bristles without the long drying time. However, relying on these sprays too often can damage brushes over time and they can leave behind a residue of their own, says Hart. In other words, use them sparingly and only when you absolutely need a quick clean until you’re able to do a thorough one.
The best products to clean makeup brushes

To help you get your makeup brushes as clean as possible, I asked Vosburg and Hart what types of products can be helpful. I then sourced highly-rated options within the categories they recommended. All of the products below have at least a four-star average rating from more than a thousand shoppers.

It’s gross and fascinating at the same time,” she says. “I love that I don’t have to do a bunch of scrubbing like I do with bar soaps and the residue comes off when I rinse it under the faucet. The gnarly smell is definitely the one drawback, but it’s nothing one pump of hand soap can’t take away.”
How do you clean makeup brushes?

Before you start cleaning, it helps to know what your brushes are made of, since synthetic and natural bristles need slightly different care. Vosburg breaks down those two most common types of brushes below.

Synthetic brushes: Many makeup brushes, especially foundation and lip brushes, are made with synthetic fibers. Because they’re typically used with liquid and cream products, they can hold onto oily buildup that’s tough to remove. A simple soap works well here, since it breaks down oils quickly and gets synthetic bristles clean without much effort.Natural hair brushes: Powder and eyeshadow brushes are often made with natural hair. These bristles are prone to staining from pigmented products like blush, but discoloration is normal and doesn’t mean the brush isn’t clean. Because natural hair can dry out over time, use a moisturizing soap (like a bar soap you may use on your body) or cleaner to keep the bristles soft and healthy.

Synthetic brushes: Many makeup brushes, especially foundation and lip brushes, are made with synthetic fibers. Because they’re typically used with liquid and cream products, they can hold onto oily buildup that’s tough to remove. A simple soap works well here, since it breaks down oils quickly and gets synthetic bristles clean without much effort.

Natural hair brushes: Powder and eyeshadow brushes are often made with natural hair. These bristles are prone to staining from pigmented products like blush, but discoloration is normal and doesn’t mean the brush isn’t clean. Because natural hair can dry out over time, use a moisturizing soap (like a bar soap you may use on your body) or cleaner to keep the bristles soft and healthy.
Once you know what you’re working with, follow these steps:

Choose your soap. Liquid dish soap or shampoo both work, but Vosburg prefers bar soap for natural hair brushes because it’s effective, non-drying and easy to use. “When cleaning with a bar of soap, I will simply wet the tips of the brush hairs with a bit of lukewarm water and then swirl the brush a few times on the bar of soap.” There are also plenty of effective cleansers on the market made specifically for makeup brushes.Work the soap into a lather. After swirling the brush on the bar or adding soap to the bristles, move it to the palm of your hand or on a silicone cleaning pad and continue swirling until it lathers. If you’re using liquid soap, a pea-size amount in your palm is enough for any size brush since it’s concentrated, says Hart. Gently wipe the brush back and forth through the soap, taking care not to press or bend the bristles too hard. Rinse. Hold the brush with the bristles pointing down and run only the brush hairs under lukewarm water. Hot water can damage the hair and loosen the glue that holds the bristles in place, says Hart. Try to keep water away from the ferrule, the metal piece that connects the bristles to the handle, since that’s where the glue and binders are. Not dunking or soaking your brushes will help reduce shedding and help them last longer, according to Vosburg.Repeat as needed. Continue lathering and rinsing until the water runs clear and the brush is free of makeup.Remove excess water and dry. Gently squeeze the bristles with a microfiber towel to remove excess water, then lay the brush flat to air dry.

Choose your soap. Liquid dish soap or shampoo both work, but Vosburg prefers bar soap for natural hair brushes because it’s effective, non-drying and easy to use. “When cleaning with a bar of soap, I will simply wet the tips of the brush hairs with a bit of lukewarm water and then swirl the brush a few times on the bar of soap.” There are also plenty of effective cleansers on the market made specifically for makeup brushes.

Work the soap into a lather. After swirling the brush on the bar or adding soap to the bristles, move it to the palm of your hand or on a silicone cleaning pad and continue swirling until it lathers. If you’re using liquid soap, a pea-size amount in your palm is enough for any size brush since it’s concentrated, says Hart. Gently wipe the brush back and forth through the soap, taking care not to press or bend the bristles too hard.

Rinse. Hold the brush with the bristles pointing down and run only the brush hairs under lukewarm water. Hot water can damage the hair and loosen the glue that holds the bristles in place, says Hart. Try to keep water away from the ferrule, the metal piece that connects the bristles to the handle, since that’s where the glue and binders are. Not dunking or soaking your brushes will help reduce shedding and help them last longer, according to Vosburg.
Repeat as needed. Continue lathering and rinsing until the water runs clear and the brush is free of makeup.
Remove excess water and dry. Gently squeeze the bristles with a microfiber towel to remove excess water, then lay the brush flat to air dry.
Frequently asked questions

With proper cleaning and care, high quality makeup brushes can last for decades, so you shouldn’t need to replace them often, according to Hart. Still, there are a few signs that it’s time for a replacement. If the glue holding the bristles to the handle starts to loosen, the brush will shed excessively, says Hart. Bristles can also flatten and fray over time, especially if you press too hard on your skin when applying makeup. Either issue means the brush should be replaced.

It’s also worth watching for bristles that break in half, which can signal that the hairs have become damaged from dehydration or overuse, according to Vosburg. Broken bristles can lead to a scratchy or uneven application, so that’s another sign it’s time to swap in a new brush.

Makeup sponges can be cleaned much like brushes, according to Hart. Start by wetting the sponge until it’s fully saturated, then swirl it on a bar of soap until it’s coated and work it into a lather in the palm of your hand, says Vosburg. Give it a few squeezes, then rinse it under warm water until no soap remains. Sponges tend to hold onto a lot of product, so you may need to repeat the lathering and rinsing several times before the water runs clear.

Once it’s clean, squeeze out any excess water and let the sponge air dry completely. Avoid storing sponges in a sealed bag or anywhere without steady airflow, since they retain moisture and can grow bacteria and mold if they can’t dry out, says Hart. “I keep my sponges and puffs in a mesh bag, so they’re constantly being aired out while in storage,” he says.
Powder puffs need to be cleaned just as often as your sponges and brushes to keep bacteria and germs from building up, says Hart.

Start by soaking the puff in warm water, then lather it with bar soap or a makeup brush cleanser. With bar soap, you can swirl the puff on the bar and work it into a lather just as you would a sponge or brush. With liquid soap, place a small amount in the center of the puff, fold it in half like a taco and rub the two sides together, according to Vosburg. Squeeze and rinse the puff under warm water, repeating as needed until it’s clean.
To dry, squeeze out the excess water and lay the puff flat. For even better airflow, set it on a kitchen drying rack or something similar so air can circulate all the way around it, says Hart.
